mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced policy uncertainty and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market and supply-side pressure, which tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: During the trigger month, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive and exceed the prior month's average by at least 1.5 percentage points (one-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% accompanied by a sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects resilient consumer and housing demand.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% in a month AND HOUST increases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window following the trigger, the cumulative 20-day forward return is negative and less than the prior 60-day average (cumulative t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 3% in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) over two months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals persistent supply-side contraction and reduced economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During the two-month contraction window, all 20-day forward returns are positive and exceed the pre-contraction average by at least 1.0 percentage point (one-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 is expected to post a positive 5-day forward return as the labor market tightening is interpreted as a sign of economic strength.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL increases by <0.2% over the same period
regime_hint: labor market tightening without inflationary pressure
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, the forward return is negative or the signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in a two-sample test versus the prior 5-day average.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual, a sharp drop in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market tightness and wage growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.5 percentage points in a single month below 4.0%
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for lagged S&P 500 returns and macroeconomic variables (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining retail sales (implied proxy via negative HOUST) combined with a sustained decline in consumer confidence (not directly observable, but as a counterfactual, a sharp drop in PAYEMS) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to persistent demand weakness.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >3% in a month AND PAYEMS decreases by >5% in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, all 20-day forward returns are positive and the cumulative 60-day return exceeds the prior 60-day average by at least 2.0 percentage points (cumulative t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 262 for three months) without a corresponding increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 is expected to show negative 20-day forward returns as the market anticipates future rate hikes and inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 262 for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS remains below 1.0% over the same period
failure_condition: Over the three-month inflation window, all 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant at the 1% level versus the pre-inflation period (two-tailed test).
